body:
>Meshes are not listed when using Compatibility. This makes the total memory usage look lower than it really is compared to other rendering methods. This should either be implemented, or a message should be added somewhere when using Compatibility to tell the user that meshes aren't tracked in the video RAM profiler.

I added a notice tooltip about meshes not being tracked in compatibility as well as buffer memory (in both)

>Since meshes now have an icon displayed next to them, textures should also have a texture icon to ensure alignment. I'd probably use Texture2D for this, but perhaps Cubemap and CubemapArray can be used when relevant.

There was a bug when porting the profiler from godot 3 to godot 4 (Texture was renamed to Texture2D), I updated the code so it now shows the proper resource icon.

>There are a lot of unnamed entries with few vertices – sometimes even 0 vertices, amounting to 0 bytes. Should we hide entries that amount to 0 bytes from the list?

 I noticed that as well, so I've made mesh entries with no path and no VRAM usage hidden.

>This also occasionally happens with textures, at least in Compatibility: Also note the bottommost entry that matches the viewport resolution and is listed at 0 bytes. Is this a reference to the swapchain being held? I'd expect it to take about 3 MB of VRAM (1152*648*4).

I’m not sure what’s going on there. I don’t use Compatibility mode and didn’t modify any of the existing texture-related code (at the time you tested this), so whatever issue this is, it’s not related to this PR.
